excerpt: you’ll need to add Corporation Tax services to your business tax account. You will then be able to manage your Corporation Tax online.
You’ll need to register your company with Companies House. You’ll get the option to be set up for Corporation Tax at the same time.
You can choose to register for VAT if your turnover is less than £90,000 (‘voluntary registration’).
You can apply for a registration ‘exception’ if your taxable turnover goes over the threshold temporarily.

If you're a sole trader or landlord, use the online service to sign up for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.
You can sign up for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax before you need to use it to help you get ready. You can sign up for the current tax year or the next one.
If you use an agent, they can sign you up instead.
Once you’re using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, you’ll add these into your compatible software before you submit your tax return.

Registration thresholds are published as exact figures: you must register for VAT when "your total taxable turnover for the last 12 months goes over £90,000", and voluntary registration below the threshold is stated on the same page.
The core corporation-tax rail is online through the business tax account: register, add Corporation Tax services, and "You will then be able to manage your Corporation Tax online."

Making Tax Digital is a sanctioned software channel stated on the sign-up page itself: filing runs through "software that works with Making Tax Digital for Income Tax", with the software-provider check called out before sign-up.
The delegated rail is one published sentence: "If you use an agent, they can sign you up instead." — agents hold their own sign-up path and client-authorisation request links.
